title: Scaffold-Type Structure Dental Ceramics with Different Compositions Evaluated through Physicochemical Characteristics and Biosecurity Profiles
authors: Fabricky MMC, Gabor AG, Milutinovici RA, Watz CG, Avram Ș, Drăghici G, Mihali CV, Moacă EA, Dehelean CA, Galuscan A, Buzatu R, Duma VF, Negrutiu ML , Sinescu C. Materials (Basel). 2021 Apr 27;14(9):2266. doi: 10.3390/ma14092266.
supports: Pre-clinical study from the botiss cerabone (sintered bovine bone) literature list — the product featured in it, which is not the same as the study being about the product, so check the design and the comparator before citing it as product evidence. Abstract, verbatim (no separate conclusion section): “The design and development of ceramic structures based on 3D scaffolding as dental bone substitutes has become a topic of great interest in the regenerative dentistry research area. In this regard, the present study focuses on the development of two scaffold -type structures obtained from differen t commercial dental ceramics by employing the foam replication method. At the same time, the study underlines the physicochemical features and the biological profiles of the newly developed scaffolds, compared to two traditional Cerabone® materials used for bone augmentation, by employing both the in vitro Alamar blue proliferation test at 24, 48 and 96 h poststimulation and the in ovo chick chorioallantoic membrane (CAM) assay. The data reveal that the newly developed scaffolds express comparable results with the traditional Cerabone® augmentation masses.
